title: Earnings per share (EPS)
definition: Profit attributable to common shareholders divided by the relevant share count. Diluted EPS accounts for instruments that could create additional shares. Compare reported and adjusted figures separately.

title: Price-to-earnings ratio (P/E)
definition: Share price divided by earnings per share. Trailing P/E uses historical earnings; forward P/E uses estimates. A low ratio can reflect weak growth or unusually high cyclical profits rather than a bargain.

title: Free cash flow
definition: Cash generated by operations after capital expenditure, subject to the definition used. Check the cash-flow statement and adjustments rather than treating earnings as cash.

title: Earnings guidance
definition: Management’s outlook for future business performance. Guidance is uncertain and can change. Compare it with prior guidance and clearly dated market expectations.

title: Market capitalization
definition: Share price multiplied by outstanding shares. It measures equity value, not enterprise value or the cash required to acquire a business.

title: Support and resistance
definition: Price areas traders watch for changes in buying or selling pressure. They describe historical behavior and can fail; they are not guaranteed floors or ceilings.

title: Risk and reward
definition: A comparison of potential loss and gain under explicit scenarios. Position size, probability, liquidity and the possibility of gaps matter as much as a target price.

title: Diversification
definition: Spreading exposure across investments with different risks. Correlations can rise during stress, so diversification reduces some risks without eliminating losses.
